slot.brief: For a xenon fluoride (e.g. XeF4), determine the number of lone pairs on xenon, its hybridisation and the shape of the molecule.

stem: For $\text{XeF}_4$, the number of lone pairs on xenon, its hybridisation and the molecular shape are

verdicts.working: Xe has 8 valence electrons. Four Xe–F bonds leave 2 lone pairs on Xe, giving 6 electron domains: sp³d² hybridisation and square-planar molecular shape.

working:
Xe has $8$ valence electrons; four Xe–F bonds leave $4$ nonbonding electrons on Xe.\nThus Xe has $2$ lone pairs and steric number $6$.\nHybridisation: $sp^3d^2$; shape: square planar.

Independent check: Xe has 8 valence electrons. Four Xe–F bonds leave 2 lone pairs on Xe, giving 6 electron domains: sp³d² hybridisation and square-planar molecular shape.
solution:
Xe has $8$ valence electrons; in $\text{XeF}_4$, four Xe–F bonds leave two lone pairs on xenon.
$$\text{Steric number}=4+2=6\;\Rightarrow\;sp^3d^2$$
The two lone pairs occupy opposite positions, giving a square-planar molecular shape.
